original_test_intent: Determine whether refreshing the relevant BMC browser context preserves the authorized session on the same target and role; the title additionally implies an active remote KVM console session whose continuity may need to survive the BMC Web Refresh/F5 operation.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM client builds and approved test account; establish an independent recovery account; record authenticated target, role and session identifiers without secrets; if title coverage is authoritative, launch one benign KVM session and capture its connected host/video state; execute the product Refresh action once and record web and KVM states; execute browser F5 once and record them again; ensure no form resubmission, target switch, duplicate KVM connection or credential exposure; close or retain sessions according to the approved final-state policy.
manual_activity: An operator supplies the authorized browser/KVM session and confirms visible target, role and console continuity; automation may apply Refresh/F5 and collect non-secret state after the intended scope is resolved.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware, WebUI build, supported browser and KVM client/version
Decision whether scope is BMC Web authentication only, active KVM-console continuity, or two explicit checkpoints
Dedicated test account/role, session timeout/renewal/CSRF expectations and permitted concurrent-session count
Exact meanings/order of WebUI Refresh versus browser F5, non-secret state oracle, final session state and independent recovery account
safety_requirements: Verify the same BMC/SUT/role before and after each operation
Use a dedicated non-production test session and preserve a separate recovery/admin path
Do not record cookies, tokens, passwords or sensitive console content
Ensure Refresh/F5 does not resubmit a state-changing form or create unintended duplicate sessions
Stop on wrong target/role, logout, CSRF/error, KVM disconnect, form resubmission or access fault; do not retry credentials blindly
agent_execution_scope: Capture non-secret DOM/page/KVM connection markers before and after each approved refresh operation
Correlate visible target and role with BMC session/audit entries
Report web-authentication and KVM-console outcomes separately when both are required
Do not expose tokens, infer an active KVM from a Web login, resubmit a form, brute-force login or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve title/body scope and whether an active KVM connection must remain established
Approve precise Refresh and F5 sequence plus authenticated/KVM persistence oracle and timeout
Approve account role, concurrent-session/final-state policy and recovery path
Review discrepancies and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Browser Refresh/F5 directly tests the Procedure and Criteria's BMC Web login persistence, but it does not create or observe the KVM session named by the title.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved browser context to capture same-target authentication before/after product Refresh and F5; if KVM is authoritative, keep one mapped console session open and separately record its connection/video/input-safe state across both operations.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC Web login, Refresh then F5, persistence check, KVM title coverage pending clarification and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model authentication and KVM-console continuity as distinct observable sessions, correlate each with the same BMC/SUT, and compare their state across the two named browser actions without collecting secret tokens.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit title/body scope, separate session oracles, same-target identity, CSRF/form safety, audit correlation and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Remaining logged into BMC Web does not prove that an already launched KVM channel stayed connected; conversely, a surviving KVM websocket does not prove the main Web session remains authenticated.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Browser refresh behavior can differ between the main BMC page, embedded KVM frame and standalone console window, and session renewal may intentionally rotate tokens while preserving authorization.

project_override_considerations: If the title is a naming defect and only BMC Web persistence is required, approve that decision while preserving Master. If KVM is required, define whether display continuity alone is sufficient or whether a harmless bounded input/heartbeat is needed; never type into an unsafe host screen.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/WebUI/browser/KVM client and test-account role identity
Non-secret before/after target, role, authenticated-page and session-status evidence
When required, mapped KVM connection/video state before and after each operation
BMC session/audit timestamps and proof of no form resubmission or duplicate session
Secret-redaction/cleanup record, recovery events and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items names KVM session status, while Procedure and Criteria only verify that the BMC Web user stays logged in after Refresh/F5 and never launch or observe KVM. These are distinct session layers, so one cannot be assumed to cover the other.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Both potential checks are technically clear and feasible once engineering selects the authoritative scope. The ambiguity is a review-layer decision rather than an unsafe irreducible execution blocker.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2237 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00019-V001: decide whether authoritative coverage is BMC Web authentication persistence, an active KVM-console session surviving Refresh/F5, or two separate checkpoints; approve BMC/SUT/WebUI/browser/KVM versions, account/role/concurrency and timeout/CSRF semantics, exact product Refresh versus browser F5 sequence, same-target visible persistence oracle, harmless KVM-state check, token redaction, cleanup and recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves the stated refresh actions while preventing BMC Web authentication from being silently substituted for the title's distinct KVM-session continuity requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: BMC Web authentication commonly uses an HTTP cookie/session, while KVM may use a separate websocket, token and native or HTML5 client lifecycle. Refreshing the parent page can preserve one and terminate or recreate the other. Therefore evidence must name which layer is under test and cannot rely on a generic 'still logged in' observation. The actions are low mutation but still need user/account context because they manipulate a live management session and can accidentally resubmit forms or expose authentication artifacts.
